title: Sales/CS enterprise ask catalog and solution navigator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable Sales/CS-facing catalog and lightweight "solution navigator" to aggregate incoming enterprise feature asks (non-bug), produce concise initial scoping (cost, effort tier, security/regulatory flags), and return a prioritized, account-aware packet to Sales/CS within 5 business days. The deliverable should be a short, searchable catalog + a one-pager solution scaffold per request that helps PM/ENG/Design rapidly decide: proceed to discovery, prototype, or decline. Focus is on repeatability, low-friction data capture, and clear hand-offs to engineering or Solutions. This ticket scopes the MVP process, templates, scoring heuristics, and integration points with Linear and the Customer Intake dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Catalog template exists and is accessible in Confluence with examples (3 sample aggregated asks)

A2: Solution navigator one-pager template (<=1 page) defined with required fields: problem statement, value, estimated effort tier (L/M/H), affected infra (hosted/dedicated/private), security/regulatory flags, and recommended next-step
A3: Scoring rubric defined and documented (value, technical complexity, account strategic score) with threshold rules for Fast-Track / Needs-Discovery / Decline
A4: Process documented for Sales/CS to submit requests (form link) and expected SLAs (5 business days for initial packet), and a notification template for customer-facing responses
A5: Hand-off checklist for ENG/Design created with required artifacts and labeling conventions for Linear tickets and dependencies
tasks: Draft catalog fields and solution navigator template
Run 3 sample consolidations (from recent Sales/CS folder) and produce example one-pagers
Sync with Solutions Engineering for account-prioritization inputs
Align scoring rubric with Go-to-Market (growth & enterprise leads)
Create intake form (Typeform/Gsheet) and automation to create Linear stub
Circulate templates for review: PM, ENG runtimes, Design, Security
Publish Confluence page and link to CS playbook
Measure initial SLA adherence and adjust process after first 10 asks

decisions: Decision 1: Use a one-page solution navigator for initial scoping instead of a long PRD to keep SLAs achievable
Decision 2: Score combines three axes (customer value, technical complexity, account strategic importance) with threshold rules for fast-track
Decision 3: Intake automation will create a Linear stub assigned to PM-queue; engineering will not be auto-assigned unless score passes 'Needs-Discovery' threshold
